claim: No priority claim is made. These are precedents/categories used to delimit the M3 contribution.

references.citation: K.M.J. de Bontridder et al., Approximation algorithms for the test cover problem, Mathematical Programming 98 (2003) 477-492.
references.overlap: Pairwise world distinction by selected tests.
references.m3_boundary: M3 adds experiment-specific costs, tolerance/noise stress and failure robustness to a preserved simulator instance; it does not claim the Test Cover formulation.

references.citation: L.A. Wolsey, An analysis of the greedy algorithm for the submodular set covering problem, Combinatorica 2 (1982) 385-393.
references.overlap: Classical greedy analysis for submodular cover with nonuniform costs.
references.m3_boundary: Applicable only when M3 is reduced to a valid coverage/submodular regime; not transferred to connected/minimax objectives.

references.citation: Daniel Golovin and Andreas Krause, Adaptive Submodularity: Theory and Applications in Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization, JAIR 42 (2011) 427-486.
references.overlap: Sequential selection with outcome uncertainty and adaptive greedy guarantees under structural assumptions.
references.m3_boundary: M3's present certification is nonadaptive finite-panel selection; no adaptive-submodularity claim.

references.citation: James B. Orlin, Andreas S. Schulz, Rajan Udwani, Robust monotone submodular function maximization, Mathematical Programming 172 (2018) 505-537.
references.overlap: Optimization under multiple submodular objective scenarios.
references.m3_boundary: Robust submodular optimization is established; M3's connected objective need not be submodular and its exact finite solver does not claim novelty.

references.citation: Shao-Lun Tang, Robust Adaptive Submodular Maximization, INFORMS Journal on Computing (2023).
references.overlap: Robustness and adaptivity under submodular structure.
references.m3_boundary: Precedent for robust adaptive design; M3 does not transfer its guarantees to the non-submodular connectivity objective.

references.citation: Q.-S. Hua et al., Dynamic programming based algorithms for set multicover and multiset multicover problems, Theoretical Computer Science (2010).
references.overlap: Redundant coverage requirements relevant to robustness against failed tests.
references.m3_boundary: M3 uses explicit one-failure minimax enumeration rather than claiming a new multicover result.

references.citation: Bernardetta Addis, Marco Di Summa, Andrea Grosso, Identifying critical nodes in undirected graphs: Complexity results and polynomial algorithms for bounded treewidth, Discrete Applied Mathematics 161 (2013) 2349-2360.
references.overlap: Budgeted graph deletion to reduce connectivity.
references.m3_boundary: M3 decision variables are experiments inducing deletion sets and a truth-rooted component score.

references.citation: Siqian Shen and J. Cole Smith, Polynomial-time algorithms for solving a class of critical node problems on trees and series-parallel graphs, Networks 60 (2012) 103-119.
references.overlap: Exact algorithms exploiting graph structure beyond trees.
references.m3_boundary: Supports looking for structural exact solvers; no equivalence or priority claim.

references.citation: Kevin T. Kennedy et al., Nodal interdiction, Mathematical and Computer Modelling 54 (2011) 3116-3125.
references.m3_boundary: Generic interdiction precedent; M3 uses response-induced experiment deletions and a distinguished truth root.

references.citation: Xu et al., A new input design framework for asymptotic active fault diagnosis with application to integrated diagnosis and control, Automatica (2024).
references.overlap: Choosing informative inputs to discriminate competing fault/model hypotheses.
references.m3_boundary: Active diagnosis is an established neighboring field; M3 makes no priority claim for experiment design for hypothesis discrimination.
